Почему отработать Speaking самостоятельно под силу только истинному Джедаю?
⠀
Если у вас развит тайм-менеджмент и you are rather good at self-discipline, вы можете обойтись без дополнительных занятий и отработать необходимые для владения английским языком навыки:
⠀
✅Reading - ресурсов на любую тему более, чем достаточно: уровень, объем (#tldr или #meme), любой жанр.
⠀
✅Listening -  YouTube, Netflix, и что греха таить: digital piracy никуда не делось, поэтому посмотреть в оригинале по-прежнему можно абсолютно всё. Смотри и прокачивай listening skills.
⠀
✅Writing - можно и с эссе повозиться, а можно написать твит, пост или комментарии к видео in English. Пишешь, просишь chat gpt проверить и объяснить ошибки. После этого принимаешь обратную связь во внимание и пишешь в следующий раз уже более sophisticated version.
⠀
❗️А вот speaking - дело коварное: нельзя прокачать speaking без real speaking. Вот почему:
⠀
📌Speaking это не только интеллектуальная деятельность, это ещё и физическая активность. Да-да, если вы понимаете, что значит "язык не слушается", то вам ясно, о чем я. Точно так же, как нельзя научиться играть в теннис или танцевать без практики, то и отработать speaking нельзя "про себя".
⠀
📌Часто бывает, что ребята, у которых довольно good command of English, путают "have/has" в разговоре, или у них вылетает глагол "to be" в потоке речи. При этом упражнения на отработку grammar они выполняют виртуозно. А всё потому, что эти нюансы не были доведены до автоматизма: и человек либо спотыкается во время беседы, либо сосредоточен на том, чтобы выразить свою мысль и допускает "неточности".
⠀
📌Что ещё тоже крайне сложно отработать или то, до чего редко доходят руки - навык задавать вопросы. Со временем мы достигаем уровня, где можем нетривиально и грамматически верно выразить своё мнение. Но как только мы пытаемся задать вопрос, начинается мешанина из вспомогательных глаголов. Кому-то сложно придумать, что спросить человека, чтобы поддержать small talk и заполнить неловкую паузу. Или когда знаешь, что спросить, но не хватает словарного запаса, и уповаешь на то, что собеседник поймёт тебя на лету.

5 Helpful Tips for Web Developers in a Remote Office:👩🏼‍💻👇

• Optimize Your Workspace Setup: 🖥️

When it comes to setting up my remote office, I like to keep things minimal but essential. Personally, I bring along Logitech's MX Keys S Keyboard and MX Anywhere 3S Mouse from the @logitech Master Series. They provide me with a comfortable typing experience and multi-device support, boosting my productivity and efficiency. 💪

• Embrace Time Management Techniques: ⏰

One method that has worked wonders for me is the Pomodoro Technique, where I divide my work into timed intervals. Additionally, I make use of helpful tools like time-tracking apps and website blockers to maintain my focus. Even if I'm in a coworking space or a laptop-friendly cafe, I create my own workstation to ensure a productive environment. 🚀

• Utilize Productivity Tools: ⚙️

Customizable Smart Actions in the Logi Options+ Software have been instrumental in effectively organizing my tasks. I've personalized certain keys to quickly access frequently used functions. For instance, I assigned the middle button on my mouse to open my favorite browser. It's become my go-to feature! I also use ready-made templates to optimize my working routine, for example a “Morning Setup” template will open up all the apps you need to start your day. 🔧

• Continuously Update Your Skill Set: 📚

Focus on 1-2 technologies at a time and prioritize understanding their underlying principles instead of memorizing the things on the surface. This approach could help you become a well-rounded professional, allowing you to go beyond relying solely on frameworks. 🌟

• Foster Work-Life Balance: ⚖️

Establish clear boundaries by defining specific working hours for your remote office. Create a routine that includes breaks, exercise, and personal hobbies. Remember, a happy developer is a productive developer! ⛱️

😀 Share your thoughts in the comments! ✍️

🚀 Case Study - Boosting Website Speed with JavaScript & Frontend Performance Optimization

👉 Did you know that a 1-second delay in page load can reduce conversions by 7%? One of the biggest challenges for Shopify & eCommerce brands today is slow, unoptimized websites caused by heavy JavaScript and poor frontend practices.

🔍 In this case study, we analyzed how frontend performance optimization + modern JavaScript frameworks can

Reduce bounce rate by 25%
Improve Core Web Vitals scores (LCP, CLS, FID)
Increase conversion rates on product pages

💡 Solution - By implementing lazy loading, minified JS/CSS, CDN integration and lightweight frameworks, we improved page speed from 5.4s → 1.7s for an eCommerce client.

✨ The result?

+42% user retention
+35% increase in sales
Better Google rankings with improved SEO performance

👉 If you’re a Shopify or eCommerce business owner, optimizing your frontend isn’t optional, it’s the key to scaling.

🔗 Let’s talk about making your website faster, smarter and more profitable.

🕵️‍♂️ “Everyone’s a web developer these days…”
But how do you really tell the pros from the pretenders?

Here are 5 red flags to help you spot a fake developer 👇

1️⃣ Page Builder Overload
If their portfolio is just drag-and-drop templates using Wix, Squarespace or Elementor, you’re paying for copy-paste, not craftsmanship.

2️⃣ No Code Standards
Ask them if they use Git, SCSS, Gulp, or any kind of version control. If they say “what’s that?”, run.

3️⃣ Can’t Explain Their Process
A real developer can walk you through their build process, from discovery to deployment. A faker will give vague answers or buzzwords.

4️⃣ No SEO or Performance Thinking
Good devs build fast, optimised sites with SEO in mind. Bad ones ignore it all and blame Google.

5️⃣ No Customisation Skills
If they can't build without 10 plugins or “need a plugin for that” they’re not a developer, they’re a WordPress plugin stacker.

Real code (not just templates)

A clean, secure web stack

A web designer is a graphic artist who develops and styles objects for the Internet. Website designers are able to tap into their creative energy and design the overall layout and look for websites.

A web developer is one that develops applications and functionality for the Internet. It is rare to find a web developer that knows every programming language; web developers usually just focus on a few languages.

Typically one developer will focus on the front end programming of a site using HTML, CSS and JavaScript while another developer will focus on server side programming like PHP, Java, Ruby, and .NET.

90% of my instagram friends know me as a tennis player. However, 50% of my soul is dedicated to computer. ⠀⠀
⠀⠀
😂 Actually this is how I got married. Julia thought all IT guys are rich)) Joking) Also she thought that if I am related with IT I can hack anyones account, does her brother’s computer science homework or repair her MacBook. ⠀⠀
⠀⠀
NOPE! A bit later I will describe you the IT profession, but today I’m going to tel you HOW DID I BECOME AN IT GUY.⠀⠀
⠀⠀
💻Part 1:⠀⠀
⠀⠀
It has all started when I was 12 when I was addicted to Counter-Strike, playing the game and surfing the Internet for new maps and skins, and communicating with “colleagues” in different forums.⠀⠀
⠀⠀
One of my “teammates” was the moderator of such website with some downloadable stuff and forum. And when I found out that the website was making money on ads and someone was offering to buy it for a couple thousand lats (Latvian currency) I got an idea why not to try to create something similar by myself? ⠀⠀
⠀⠀
I heard already something about website builders/CMS, SEO (at least knew the term) and in general I was active, communicative player, so kinda had all skills at least to try... ⠀⠀
⠀⠀
My first website was build on uCoz (website builder) and it was about Counter-Strike 1.6 and uCoz (downloading templates, etc). I have installed some template, created forum, fulfilled it with content, added many files with unique description, made basic SEO and started to promote the site in other forums. ⠀⠀
⠀⠀
After half year of managing site it has reached total of 2000 users, 500 visitors per day (mostly from search engines) and I’ve sold it for 600 lats (around 900 euros). For me, 12-13 years old guy, that was a success! 💰 💰 💰 ⠀⠀
⠀⠀
The only my investment was hosting, which cost around 2 eur per month. This is how I’ve started my “entrepreneurship” and connection to IT. ⠀⠀
⠀⠀
To be continued...⠀⠀
⠀⠀

A web developer is one that develops applications and functionality for the Internet. It is rare to find a web developer that knows every programming language; web developers usually just focus on a few languages.

Speaker Announcement: 'Building Powerful Subscription And Membership Sites That Scale' - Presented by Ben May from https://thecode.co/ and Adrian O'Hagan from https://www.crikey.com.au/

Subscription revenue models are an increasingly popular choice for a lot of different types of businesses -- more and more websites are exploring partial or total subscription strategies.

Speakers Adrian O’Hagan from Crikey and Private Media, and Ben May from The Code Company share their experiences in building and migrating large complex WordPress subscription sites.

Two unique perspectives; Adrian’s experience as both product manager and developer, and Ben as a technical agency working with clients on these kinds of projects.

This talk will examine some of the common pain points experienced with scaling subscription sites, and how the pair have architected powerful and flexible subscription sites using SaaS products such as Chargify.

We are learning WordPress in school and working on a few projects. I'm working on an e-commerce project and a personal blog site. WordPress feels cheesey at times, but you can build some incredible sites with no coding skills.

The blog is aiming towards helping new developers, as I struggle when I first began coding, which was about a year ago. I have 2 toddlers so my time is not as flexible.

•

⭐️The Freedom and Luxury of being Self Employed⭐️

Happy Hump Day IG fam 🐪

I was so busy today that as you can see i’ve only just sat down to work (7pm).
Becoming self employed was/is one of the best decisions i’ve made. 
-
The best part about it is that YOU decide when to work and when not to work. Don’t get me wrong, I loved being part of a big company but the thing I hated the most was always having to ask permission from someone in order to be able to take a day off, or potentially leave early from work.
-
I am my own boss now and I decide my own fate. If I have things to do during the day (like today) I will do them and then catch up on my work in the evening. I’m probably going to be here until really late tonight but as long as I get everything I want done then to me that’s a successful working session.
-
So here’s my question to you, if you had the choice/luxury would you go Self Employed or would you rather work for someone else?
-
Let me know 👇🏻

This past week, I fought a frustrating battle.
One of my clients runs a large e-commerce website — we’re talking hundreds of thousands of files. We needed to migrate the site to a new web host. 

On the surface, web file migration should be simple, but a low disk space issue turned it into a nightmare.

From Monday to Friday, I struggled. I tried downloading files manually, one by one, arranging them in folders on my local machine — a process so tedious, it almost broke me.

I tried using the All-in-One WP Migration plugin, but it couldn’t handle the backup due to insufficient storage. Every attempt seemed to hit a wall.

By Friday morning, I was exhausted… but I refused to quit.

I took a breath and decided to try again. This time, I turned to a plugin I had dismissed in the past: UpdraftPlus. I didn’t like it at first use, but with more experience, I’ve come to realize it’s one of the most reliable free backup and migration plugins out there.

To my surprise, it backed up everything — flawlessly.

Not only that, but it also allowed me to delete the downloaded files afterward to free up space and complete the job.

But this story isn’t really about WordPress or migration tools.
It’s about something deeper — the power of faith, resilience, and innovation.

👉🏾 Faith to believe a solution exists.
👉🏾 Resilience to keep going even after repeated failure.
👉🏾 Innovation to try a different route when the usual ones don’t work.

Sometimes, your breakthrough isn’t in a brand-new idea — it’s in giving an old idea a second chance with a fresh perspective.

If you’re stuck right now, just know: you’re one plugin, one new try, or one mindset shift away from winning.
.
.
.
.
.

This past week, I fought a frustrating battle.
One of my clients runs a large e-commerce website — we’re talking hundreds of thousands of files. We needed to migrate the site to a new web host. 

On the surface, web file migration should be simple, but a low disk space issue turned it into a nightmare.

From Monday to Friday, I struggled. I tried downloading files manually, one by one, arranging them in folders on my local machine — a process so tedious, it almost broke me.

I tried using the All-in-One WP Migration plugin, but it couldn’t handle the backup due to insufficient storage. Every attempt seemed to hit a wall.

By Friday morning, I was exhausted… but I refused to quit.

I took a breath and decided to try again. This time, I turned to a plugin I had dismissed in the past: UpdraftPlus. I didn’t like it at first use, but with more experience, I’ve come to realize it’s one of the most reliable free backup and migration plugins out there.

To my surprise, it backed up everything — flawlessly.

Not only that, but it also allowed me to delete the downloaded files afterward to free up space and complete the job.

But this story isn’t really about WordPress or migration tools.
It’s about something deeper — the power of faith, resilience, and innovation.

👉🏾 Faith to believe a solution exists.
👉🏾 Resilience to keep going even after repeated failure.
👉🏾 Innovation to try a different route when the usual ones don’t work.

Sometimes, your breakthrough isn’t in a brand-new idea — it’s in giving an old idea a second chance with a fresh perspective.

If you’re stuck right now, just know: you’re one plugin, one new try, or one mindset shift away from winning.

Latest addition to the setup, the Microsoft Surface Ergonomic Keyboard. I wanted to avoid the flashy gamer setup trend, and go with a modern minimalist and unique design. Not bad for $55 price tag on eBay.
√
I'm still working on the dual screens, currently doing my homework on the right sizes and recommend features. I'm leaning toward the dual setup instead of the ultrawide monitors. I like snapping windows, and I can't see that working properly on an ultrawide monitor.

We are learning WordPress in school and working on a few projects. I'm working on an e-commerce project and a personal blog site. WordPress feels cheesey at times, but you can build some incredible sites with no coding skills.
•
The blog is aiming towards helping new developers, as I struggle when I first began coding, which was about a year ago. I have 2 toddlers so my time is not as flexible.
•
I would wake up at 4:30AM to study while attending a coding bootcamp in UCSD. It was fucking intense. I had zero programing experience, but I loved how it stimulated my problem solving aptness. It also helped me cope with my PTSD which quickly became almost non-existent.
•
I feel grateful for being in this profession. The community is amazing, plus there is always something new to try and learn.

Web development is the process of creating and maintaining websites. It involves a range of tasks, including web design, front-end development, back-end development, server configuration, and database management.

1. Web design involves the visual and aesthetic aspects of a website, including layout, color scheme, typography, and user experience. Front-end development involves using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to create the user interface and user experience of a website. Back-end development involves writing server-side code, such as PHP, Python, or Ruby, to handle database interactions and website functionality. Server configuration involves setting up the server environment to support the website, including web server software and database software. Database management involves creating and managing the databases that store the website's data.

2. There are many tools and technologies used in web development, including web frameworks such as Ruby on Rails, Django, and Laravel, content management systems (CMS) such as WordPress, and e-commerce platforms such as Shopify and WooCommerce. There are also many front-end frameworks and libraries available, such as React, Angular, and Vue.js, which make it easier to build complex user interfaces and single-page applications.

3. One of the most important aspects of web development is web accessibility, which ensures that websites are usable by people with disabilities. This involves making websites accessible to people with visual, auditory, physical, and cognitive disabilities by using accessible design techniques and standards.

4. In conclusion, web development is a complex and rewarding field that requires a combination of technical and creative skills. With the right tools and techniques, web developers can create websites that are both visually appealing and highly functional, and help to meet the needs of businesses and users alike.

🔄 Understanding Flex Direction in CSS! 💻✨

Flexbox is a powerful layout tool, and flex-direction controls the direction of your items. Here’s how it works:

👉 row (default): Items are placed horizontally, left to right. 🟰➡️
👉 row-reverse: Items are placed horizontally, but right to left. ↔️
👉 column: Items are placed vertically, top to bottom. ⬇️⬇️
👉 column-reverse: Items are placed vertically, bottom to top. 🔄⬆️

🔹 Why use it?
It’s perfect for creating responsive layouts, organizing content, and maintaining flexibility across devices! 📱🎯

💡 Pro Tip: Pair flex-direction with justify-content for ultimate layout control! 💥

Which layout will you try next? Share your thoughts below! 👇

Many beginner web developers fall into the same traps and these mistakes can seriously affect the quality, usability, and scalability of a website.

One of the most common issues is ignoring mobile responsiveness. With more than half of web traffic coming from mobile devices, a site that breaks on phones can drive visitors away instantly. 

Another overlooked problem is having a messy file and folder structure, which makes the project difficult to scale and nearly impossible for teams to collaborate effectively.

Testing your site only on one browser? That’s risky. Without cross-browser testing, your design might break on other platforms, causing confusion for users.

And if you’re writing inline CSS everywhere, you’re not just cluttering your code you’re also making it harder to maintain in the long run.

Lastly, many developers forget about basic accessibility. This doesn't just hurt your SEO rankings, it makes your site difficult or even impossible to use for people with disabilities.

If you're just starting out in web development or want to clean up your workflow, understanding these common pitfalls is the first step.

Explore our in-depth breakdown of these mistakes and how to avoid them in our latest post.

Here's an explanation of the difference between a landing page and a homepage:

A landing page is a web page that is specifically designed for one main purpose, such as encouraging visitors to take a specific action—for example, signing up, purchasing a product, or filling out a form. Typically, landing pages have a very focused design and minimal distractions, without a lot of navigation or outbound links. Landing page visitors generally come from advertising, email marketing, or social media promotions.

Meanwhile, the Homepage is the main page of a website that serves as an entrance to various parts of the site. The homepage provides an overview of what a business or organization has to offer. Inside you have tons of navigation, links, and menus to other pages like products, services, blogs, and contacts. Homepages are more informative and designed for exploration, not just for one specific action.

In short, landing pages focus on one-action conversions, while homepages focus on navigation and general information.

🌐 Why Entertainment and Media Websites are Essential for Your Business 🎬

In today's digital age, having a strong online presence is crucial for success, especially in the entertainment and media industry. Here's why your business needs an impactful website:

1. 24/7 Accessibility: Your audience can access your content anytime, anywhere. This means your news, music, videos, and event details are available round the clock, catering to a global audience.

2. Enhanced User Experience: A well-designed website offers a seamless and engaging experience, keeping your visitors hooked. From streaming music and videos to reading the latest news and booking tickets, a user-friendly interface is key.

3. Brand Credibility: Establish your brand as a trusted and authoritative source. A professional website boosts credibility and helps you stand out in a crowded market.

1. Learn Web Development Fundamentals
The best first step is to learn which are HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

2. Choose a Specialization
At some point, you’ll need to choose an area of web development to specialize in. There are three main types:

- Front-End Developer. A Front-End Developer works on the “client-side” of web development like the site or app that users interact with.

- Back-End Developer. A Back-End Developer works on the “server-side” of web development like site functions, databases, servers, networks and hosting, etc.

- Full-Stack Developer. A Full-Stack Developer is familiar with both front-and back-end development and works with both sides of a website.

3. Learn Key Programming Languages in your Specialization
You’ll need to learn to use a handful of different programming languages for your specialization. Example: Front-End uses React, Angular, etc. Back-End uses Kotlin, PHP, etc.

4. Build Projects to Develop Your Web Developer Skills
Do some free work for your favourite brands or engage in some personal projects. This way, you can have a portfolio to show prospective clients.
